los.text: Take a relevant drug history from a patient, including prescribed, over-the-counter, and herbal medications
los.html:
Ask aboutDetail
PrescribedName, dose, frequency, route, indication, when started, who prescribed
Over the counterPainkillers (NSAIDs), antihistamines, PPIs, laxatives
Herbal / supplementsSt John's wort (enzyme inducer), ginkgo, vitamins
RecreationalDrugs, alcohol
Adherence"Many people find it hard to take all their tablets: how do you manage?"; dosette boxes, who helps
Side effectsAny problems with the medicines
AllergiesDrug and reaction (rash vs anaphylaxis vs intolerance)
Recent changesStopped, started, dose changes
  • Sources: patient, GP record, repeat slip, pharmacy, carers, medication itself (medicines reconciliation within 24 h of admission).

los.text: Explain how drug interactions can occur and identify common interaction risks.
los.html:
TypeMechanismExample
Pharmacokinetic: enzyme inhibitionLess metabolism → higher levelsClarithromycin + simvastatin (myopathy); fluconazole + warfarin
Pharmacokinetic: enzyme inductionMore metabolism → lower levelsRifampicin, carbamazepine, St John's wort reduce the pill, warfarin
AbsorptionBinding in the gutCalcium/iron reduce levothyroxine and ciprofloxacin
ExcretionReduced renal clearanceNSAIDs/ACE inhibitors raise lithium
Pharmacodynamic: additiveSame effectACE inhibitor + spironolactone (hyperkalaemia); SSRI + NSAID (bleeding); multiple sedatives
Pharmacodynamic: opposingCancel outBeta-blocker + salbutamol
"Triple whammy"NSAID + ACE inhibitor/ARB + diuretic → AKI.
High-riskWarfarin, digoxin, lithium, theophylline, phenytoin (narrow therapeutic index); older patients with polypharmacy.
CheckBNF interactions appendix, pharmacist.

los.text: Explain patients’ medication schedules using clear and appropriate language.
los.html:
TechniqueExample
Find out what they know"Which tablets do you take in the morning?"
Link each medicine to its purpose"This one protects your heart"
Timing tied to routines"With breakfast", "at bedtime"
Special instructionsAlendronate: empty stomach, upright 30 min; levothyroxine before food
AidsMedication list, chart, dosette box, pharmacy blister packs, apps
Teach-back"Talk me through how you'll take them"
Side effects to watch forAnd what to do

los.text: Describe commonly used cognitive impairment screening tools and their clinical applications.
los.html:
ToolDetailUse
AMTS (Abbreviated Mental Test Score)10 questions; <8 suggests impairmentQuick screen in hospital
4ATAlertness, AMT4, attention (months backwards), acute change; ≥4 = possible deliriumDelirium screening
MoCA (Montreal Cognitive Assessment)30 points; <26 abnormal; sensitive for mild impairmentMemory clinics
ACE-III (Addenbrooke's)100 points across 5 domainsDetailed assessment
6CIT6 items, primary careQuick screen
Mini-Cog3-word recall + clock drawingBrief screen
  • Remember: screening tools don't diagnose dementia
    • consider delirium, depression, sensory impairment, education and language
    • check bloods (B12, folate, TFTs, calcium) and refer to memory clinic.

los.text: Perform a basic cognitive assessment using an appropriate screening tool
los.html:
• AMTS questions (1 point each): age
    • time (nearest hour)
    • address for recall at the end (e.g. "42 West Street")
    • year
    • name of this place
    • recognise two people
    • date of birth
    • year WW2 started (1939)
    • name of the current monarch
    • count backwards from 20 to 1.
1Explain, consent, check hearing and glasses, quiet room.
2Ask questions exactly as written; don't prompt.
3Score and interpret in context (acute change → delirium); repeat to monitor.
4Collateral history from family or carers.

los.text: Demonstrate the ability to perform a respiratory examination with clinical competence, interpret and integrate findings with relevant knowledge to support clinical reasoning, and clearly present these findings to peers or supervisors.
los.html:
• Full routine: see ICM Year 1 › Respiratory › LOs 2 and 8.
Competence =
Fluent sequence front and back with finishing steps
Pattern recognition: consolidation, effusion, pneumothorax, collapse, fibrosis, COPD
Present a coherent summary and differential, with next steps (CXR, sats, ABG, sputum culture, spirometry)

Principle (antimicrobial stewardship)Detail
Follow local guidelinesEmpirical choice by likely organism and local resistance
Take cultures first (if possible)Blood, urine, sputum, swabs
Start promptly when neededSepsis: within 1 hour
DocumentIndication, drug, dose, route, duration or review date
Start Smart, Then FocusReview at 48–72 h: stop, switch IV to oral, change, continue, or OPAT
Narrowest spectrum, shortest effective courseReduce resistance and C. difficile
Check allergiesTrue penicillin allergy vs intolerance
Interactions and monitoringGentamicin/vancomycin levels, renal function
  • Avoid antibiotics for viral infections (e.g. influenza, colds): give self-care and safety-netting advice
    • antivirals (oseltamivir) only for at-risk groups when flu is circulating.
